deals.evidence: Finalmente, la inyección ascendió a 595 millones
deals.headline: Barça's EUR 595m refinancing placed via Goldman Sachs
deals.investor: New York Life, MetLife, Allianz, Cigna, Barings, Pricoa and Apollo (placed via Goldman Sachs)
deals.summary: After a EUR 80m Goldman Sachs bridge loan in June 2021, the club raised EUR 595m: EUR 455m of new Senior Secured Notes (average 1.98%, 10 years) and EUR 140m of refinanced bonds, with New York Life, MetLife, Allianz, Cigna, Barings, Pricoa and Apollo as investors, per Crónica Global citing the club's 2021 statement.

deals.evidence: Sixth Street will initially invest €207.5 million
deals.headline: Sixth Street buys 10% of Barça's LaLiga TV rights for 25 years for EUR 207.5m
deals.summary: First 'lever': Sixth Street invests EUR 207.5m for 10% of the club's LaLiga TV rights for 25 years; the club booked a EUR 267m capital gain for the season. Not equity in the club.

deals.evidence: En total, Sixth Street recibirá el 25% de los derechos de televisión del Club de LaLiga durante los próximos 25 años
deals.headline: Sixth Street buys a further 15% of Barça's LaLiga TV rights, taking it to 25% for 25 years
deals.summary: Second tranche: an additional 15% of the club's LaLiga TV rights, so Sixth Street receives 25% for the next 25 years. The club's release states no price.

deals.evidence: FC Barcelona announces the sale of 24.5% of Barça Studios to the company Socios.com for 100 million euros
deals.headline: Socios.com buys 24.5% of Barça Studios for EUR 100m
deals.summary: Sale of 24.5% of the club's audiovisual subsidiary Barça Studios (not of the club) to Socios.com to accelerate its audiovisual, blockchain, NFT and Web3 strategy.

deals.evidence: FC Barcelona announces the sale of 24.5% of Barça Studios to the company Orpheus Media
deals.headline: Orpheus Media buys 24.5% of Barça Studios for EUR 100m
deals.summary: Sale of a further 24.5% of the Barça Studios subsidiary to Orpheus Media, the audiovisual producer managed by Jaume Roures.

deals.evidence: The Club agreed financing with a total of 20 investors to the value of 1.450 billion Euro
deals.headline: Barça closes EUR 1.45bn Espai Barça financing with 20 investors
deals.investor: 20 investors (club's advisers included Goldman Sachs and JP Morgan)
deals.summary: Financing for the Spotify Camp Nou rebuild in tranches of 5, 7, 9, 20 and 24 years with a grace period, repaid from stadium income (forecast c. EUR 247m a year); no club assets pledged and no mortgage on the stadium.

deals.evidence: have become new partners in Bridgeburg Invest, the holding company of Barça Vision
deals.headline: Libero and NIPA-advised investors buy 29.5% of Barça Vision for EUR 120m
deals.investor: LIBERO football finance AG and private investors advised by NIPA Capital B.V.
deals.seller: Socios.com and Orpheus Media (part of their holdings)
deals.summary: The investors acquired 29.5% of Barça Vision (Bridgeburg Invest) for EUR 120m, corresponding to part of the stakes held by Socios.com and Orpheus Media; the club also signed a business combination agreement with the SPAC Mountain & Co. I for a planned Barça Media listing. Bridgeburg was merged into Barça Produccions in 2025.

deals.evidence: FC Barcelona has closed a bond issuance worth €424 million
deals.headline: Barça refinances EUR 424m of Espai Barça debt with a bond issue
deals.investor: Bond investors (Goldman Sachs as financial adviser)
deals.summary: EUR 424m of stadium debt originally due in 2028 restructured into bonds repaid from 2033 to 2050, average cost 5.19%.

deals.evidence: El Barça obtuvo un ingreso de 105 millones después de cerrar la operación con fondos de inversión y fondos de pensiones estadounidenses
deals.headline: Barça issues EUR 105m of Senior Media Notes backed by TV income
deals.investor: US investment funds and pension funds (Goldman Sachs as lead manager and placement agent)
deals.summary: First of two EUR 105m Senior Media Notes issues (10 years, 5.14% fixed) secured on LaLiga and UEFA audiovisual income; the second is planned for October-November 2026. Part of the EUR 510m package the assembly approved on 19 Sep 2026.

deals.evidence: The first consists of €300 million earmarked for completing construction work at Spotify Camp Nou
deals.headline: Members approve EUR 300m more Espai Barça financing to finish the Spotify Camp Nou
deals.investor: Espai Barça lenders (not named by the club)
deals.summary: The 2026 assembly approved a EUR 510m package: EUR 300m to complete the stadium works and EUR 210m in two Media Notes issues (recorded separately). It sits within the Espai Barça structure approved in 2023, now EUR 1.485bn.

name: Futbol Club Barcelona
notes: Revenue is the club's 'ordinary revenue' for 2025-26 (EUR 1.06bn; net result -EUR 18m; ordinary profit EUR 0.2m; net equity -EUR 168m) from the 19 Sep 2026 assembly release; the 2025-26 annual report PDF was not yet on the transparency page, so the breakdown, net debt, attendance and social figures are 2024-25 from the 2024/25 Annual Report (operating income EUR 994m, of which Stadium 175, Media 250, Commercial 473, Transfers and loans 44, Others 52, EUR m, read off the chart; 'other' excludes the 44 of transfers). Deloitte's Money League 2026 puts 2024-25 revenue at EUR 975m (2nd), including c. EUR 70m of one-off Personal Seat Licence income. EBITDA: EUR 140m in the accounts release; the EUR 510m financing release cites a projected EUR 184m for 2025-26 (different basis). Net debt (EUR 469m, LaLiga criteria) excludes Espai Barça debt. Capacity 62,652 is the partially reopened Spotify Camp Nou after phase 1C (club statement, 10 Mar 2026); the club's stadium page still shows the pre-rebuild 99,354. Pretax result and wages are not given on a clean page (the audited accounts PDF garbles digits on extraction; the annual report only gives a 'sporting wage bill' including amortisation). Forbes' own page blocks automated access, so the valuation cites BBC Sport's report of the Forbes list; the club says Forbes values it at 'more than 6.5 billion euros'. The second Sixth Street tranche (15%) has no price in the club or Sixth Street releases. Barça Produccions (Barça Media): the club's stake fell to about 53% after absorbing Bridgeburg Invest in 2025 (joint control from 2025) and rose to 63.14% in 2025-26 per Crónica Global; the partners' current split is not published. No chief executive is named on the club site. Old record's Wikipedia/Goal sources have been replaced.

owners.evidence: The club belongs to you, the Barça members
owners.name: FC Barcelona members (socis)

ownership_summary: Futbol Club Barcelona is a not-for-profit association owned by its members (socis, more than 140,000 in 2024/25), who elect the board; Joan Laporta was re-elected president on 15 March 2026. No investor holds equity in the club: institutional capital sits around it, in Sixth Street's 25% share of the club's LaLiga TV rights to 2047, minority stakes in the digital and audiovisual subsidiary Barça Produccions (Barça Media, club 63.14% per Crónica Global), and the debt that funds the Spotify Camp Nou rebuild.
